Hi Alice - great questions. High-level answers below; Rishi will add technical details. Attaching the KMS overview + our SOC2 report for your security team.

1) Replication: By default, hosted deployments keep data in the configured region. We do not replicate request logs or persisted model artifacts to other regions unless customers opt into cross-region backups or analytics. Backups are optional and can be disabled for your account.

2) Customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK): Supported in two modes depending on deployment:
   - Hosted (Redwood-managed control plane + customer project): We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP CMEK. Your CMK can be used to encrypt stored secrets; keys are never exported to Redwood. We integrate with KMS APIs so encryption/decryption operations are performed by the cloud KMS; Redwood holds only ciphertext.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): You can bring your own HSM/KMS (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM) and control key lifecycle; Redwood's runtime can be configured to use your keywrap service.

3) Deletion & retention: We provide retention policies per-project with configurable log retention windows. For PII removal, we support a deletion API that triggers purge from request logs and caches; for model-generated artifacts (e.g., embeddings) we can identify and delete records based on metadata keys. We will confirm exact SLAs for purges during the technical deep-dive.

Next steps: Rishi, can you add a short technical note covering TLS versions, at-rest encryption algorithms, KMS key usage semantics, audit logs, and suggested architecture for PayWise? Also, Alice - please attach the security questionnaire when convenient and let us know which deep-dive slot works (Tue 23 or Wed 24, PT).

Best,
Marissa

Hi Alice / Marissa - quick technical note to supplement Marissa's summary. TL;DR: we support industry-standard TLS in-transit, AES-256 at-rest, and both CMK via cloud KMS and HSM/bring-your-own-key options. Details below: 

In-transit:
- All API and inter-service traffic uses TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; we recommend TLS 1.3 for client endpoints where supported.

At-rest:
- Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Keys are envelope-encrypted with a root-KEK managed in the chosen KMS.

Customer-managed keys (options):
1) Hosted (CMEK): You grant Redwood the minimal KMS IAM permissions to Call Encrypt/Decrypt using your CMK. Redwood never stores plaintext keys; decrypt operations are performed through KMS and only transient plaintext exists in secure memory during processing. Key policies and IAM roles are scoped to reduce blast radius.
2) BYOK / HSM: For Private deployments we support integration with customer HSMs (PKCS#11 or cloud HSM). Keys never leave your HSM; Redwood performs keywrap/unwrapping through your provided keywrap service.

Key rotation & audit:
- Rotation: We recommend rotation of data encryption keys at least quarterly. KMS-driven rotation for CMKs is supported; envelope keys can be rotated with migration tooling.
- Audit logs: KMS API calls are logged to customer cloud audit logs (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs) when using customer-managed KMS. Redwood also emits internal access logs (who/which service requested decrypt). We can provide per-request audit identifiers to correlate application logs with KMS events.

Data residency & replication:
- By default, no cross-region replication of logs or persistent model artifacts. If required, we can enable cross-region backups under contractual controls.

Deletion & API:
- We expose a deletion API for request logs and persisted artifacts. Purge requests generate a job with an audit trail; expected completion depends on dataset size - typical SLA for a <100k-record purge is 48 hours. We can agree on stricter SLAs in contract.
